title: Robot Bounded In Circle
summary: On an infinite plane, a robot begins at coordinates (0, 0) facing north.
statement: On an infinite plane, a robot begins at coordinates (0, 0) facing north. It follows instructions to move or turn as follows: "G" means move forward 1 unit, "L" means turn 90 degrees to the left, and "R" means turn 90 degrees to the right. The robot repeats these instructions indefinitely. Determine if the robot's path remains within a circle of any size.
constraints: Instructions contain G, L, and R and repeat forever.
Return whether the path stays inside some circle.
reference_solution:
def robot_is_bounded(instructions):
 x=y=direction=0;moves=((0,1),(1,0),(0,-1),(-1,0))
 for command in instructions:
  if command=='G':x+=moves[direction][0];y+=moves[direction][1]
  elif command=='L':direction=(direction-1)%4
  else:direction=(direction+1)%4
 return (x,y)==(0,0) or direction!=0

hints: After one cycle, only displacement and final direction determine all later cycles.
The path is bounded if displacement is zero or orientation changed.
Simulate one instruction string from origin facing north.
A changed direction rotates repeated displacement vectors to cancel within four cycles; unchanged nonzero displacement repeats forever.
editorial: A changed direction rotates repeated displacement vectors to cancel within four cycles; unchanged nonzero displacement repeats forever.

tests.explanation: One cycle returns to the origin, so repetition is bounded.
The robot advances north every cycle without turning, so it is unbounded.
